column2: A tale of long, long ago.
On the roads that linked / the villages, monsters had
piled haunted idols high, / blocking travel, they say.
In Kamakura, at that time, / lived a young, clever monk
and a lovely shrine maiden / with great divine powers.
Since childhood, the two / had competed over every
little thing as they grew / up, or so the story goes.
One day, the head priest / and the villagers were
talking about the haunted / idols and the monsters.
The young monk, listening / in from behind, spoke up:

Everyone!! I will get rid / of those monsters for you,
msg:17.5	every last one of them!! / he said,
and before the head priest / could stop him,
off he went to fight evil / spirits and train as well.
When the shrine maiden / heard of this, not to be
outdone, she set off after / the young monk, they say.
Many ups and downs await. / How will it all turn out?

column2: Did these two get along, / or not? Who could say...
Having beaten the red oni / with ease, they raced each
other out of Kamakura, / or so the story goes.
Hey!! Stop right there!! / "Return our rice balls!!"
The story goes that the / two caught the nekomata,
made it mend its ways, / shared their rice balls
with it, and let it go.
From inside the broken / clockwork daruma came
a tiny, adorable ghost, / or so they say.
Aww! So cute! Is this / really an evil spirit?
Looks like the monsters / were using it.
The two let the ghost go, / then asked the villagers
to free the blue oni tied / to a tree later on,
and left the village / behind, they say.
What about the blue oni? / "Leave him, leave him."
Deeply sorry for all it / had done, the kappa
caught fish in the sea and / treated them to a feast.
Doesn't this make it look / like we were the bullies?

Hmm... this is awkward. / Our rice balls are back,
msg:52.3	so shall we hurry on? / "Let's go."
The nekomata siblings / offered them rice balls
to repay the ones from / before. Accepting them,
the two hurried on their / way as the siblings waved.
Those two went and ate / our fish again......
The two kappa gazed long / at the departing pair,
sorry to see them go, / or so they say.
Now the best of friends, / the three talked on and on

All I did was teach a / lesson to stuck-up humans
msg:54.4	like you!! I did nothing / wrong, I tell you.

Phew, it's finally over. / The head priest must be
msg:55.2	waiting, worried sick. / "Actually, I left without
telling my shrine master. / He must be furious."
need more training?" / "Yeah. Let's do that."
Their journey goes on / and on, but for now...
